title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: As a fan of both collectible trading card games and superheroes, Sentinels of the Multiverse hits a special sweet spot for me. The graphics are colorful and pretty. The style is authentically superhero in nature, feeling like panels lifted from a comic book. I appreciate the page turn wipe mechanic to illustrate the rotation of turns from character to character; though, this effect slows the game down, so I eventually did turn it off. Also, the animations for damage infliction have been improved since launch, which demonstrates the developers dedication to refining and expanding the game, though these quickly become tedious. The characters are diverse, as are the cards that you play to simulate their superpowers and manuevers on the battlefield. In general, the cards are well-illustrated and have great flavor text. Combining the abilities of different heroes often results in synergies that mirror a team of superpowered beings working together to defeat one arch-villain, as well as containing that random element that can make CCGs addicting by their ability to reveal combinations and pitfalls over time. I did find the characters to be wildly out of balance, with some being useful against virtually every foe and in every circumstance. While other characters require very particular draws or circumstances, or the understanding and exploitation of a self-damage mechanic to make them effective. I tended to avoid these, focusing instead on looking at the pool of abilities that the team possessed, which may well have been the focus the developers had in mind. Similarly, most of the villains are interesting puzzles to solve that present different challenges depending on your chosen cast of characters and the environment in which you do battle. However, some villains operate under a broad rule-breaking mechanic that renders a particular character almost useless, or they have one particular trick around which you have to orient and time your strategy. I felt those villains had less replay value than the more broadly accessible and understandable villains. Others may appreciate these asymmetric enemies more than I do. Fortunately, the season pass has, thus far, yielded fun additions of heroes, arch-villains and environments. If I had a criticism, I'd like to see more playable hero characters in relation to the number of arch-villains, but the mix might be sweeter to someone else's taste. The music is upbeat from the main screen and varies appropriately with the various environments; though, like the comic book page turn wipes, I did eventually turn it off. Much more quickly, I turned off the sound effects: those become repetitive almost immediately (especially the projectile damage sound effect, which gets played frequently). A major shortfall of the game is the lack of customization of individual hero decks. While variants on the various heroes and villains in the game can be opened up by meeting very specific gameplay requirements, they amount to having a single different core power. Being able to unlock and select different cards in an attempt to kit out a particular hero to face a specific enemy would have added another layer of strategic depth and might have made the more narrow villains more interesting to me. Taking into account the fast game play, the colorful illustrations, the great writing on the color text and myriad combinations of heroes, arch-villains and environment (with many more coming down the pipe) that play out in many different ways, I can't help but to give this game a total thumbs-up.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: Updated - After my intitial review of the base game listed below. I felt that the game was lacking in a few areas that have been updated. Its strange that while i initially had this game objectively listed as 5/10 as a result of playing it I went and bought the tabletop version and have become a huge fan. I am happy to say that with recent addition of the first full expansion packs as well as some slight quaility of life upgrades since the games release and my purchase I would now bump up my grade to a 6/10 and a I would recommend the digital version to most people at this point. There are still a ton of things that I feel should be added to improve the game and I still feel they should do more to animate and accentuate the game given the tools at their disposal. Multiplayer should be top of the list. I left my orginial review unaltered except for a few quick grammar corrections for any whom are on the fence about buying the game please read on..... Orginal Review After much internal debate I came to the assement that the developers managed to digitized a GREAT tabletop game...however I still have to give this the thumb downs. So to be clear...I enjoyed the mechanics, the game runs smoothly, and there seems to have a very good developer to community relationship (at least in my experience) yet I still would not recomend purchasing this game. I was disappointed to find this talbletop/card game that fails to add any compeling elements despite the fact that it has ascended into the digital world. This is a sin I cannot overlook and makes me regret not buying the tabletop version. I would say being given the keys to go anywhere and do anything at Disneyworld and then refusing to leave the parking lot does not make a bad person but it does make me wonder what end of the autism spectrum you sit. This is not a bad "game" just an unnecessarily limited "video game" and a complete waste of potential. To clarify the game itself is FUN and well designed with the different combinations of decks (heros, villians, environment) providing a good deal of variety in terms of playstyle from game to game. However there are no animations past the static comic book pieces of art (though well done at from what I can tell on par with the carboard box takehome) and very little else to help color the experience after multiple playthroughs. It may be that every game is different but it honestly does not feel much different to me. There are some very obscure conditions that allow you to unlock "variants" of particular decks (heros and villains no location unlocks) but most of that satisfaction feeling I usually get after succesfully beating a game or fufilling a condition of an unlock is absent. There is an overall lack of content here. I understand and believe that the developers where trying to be as faithful as possible to the tabletop version and they succeed in doing so here. In the end the human element that is lost by playing this game solo (no multiplayer option to attempt to replace human contact either) makes it a failure. Again this a true shame as their really is a ton of potential here. There is no progression or advancment that I can see and it lacks window dressing. All that being said I am going to purchase the tabletop game and give it a go at game night with my friends this week. Again this is a great "GAME" but a poor "VIDEO GAME" I would recommend you support the game in it's original form but skip on this version. 5/10 Tough to come up with my rating here but I will stand by it as being the perfect example of a 5. When reviewing it I did not comeup with a single good or bad point without finding a contradiction steering me in the other direction. End Original Review In case you skipped to the end in it's current state 6/10 as of April 16th 2015... 10/10 for the tabletop version of the game its still best played with friends.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: Sentinels is a very fun, very well-made game. You control a team of 3-5 comic book heroes and battle a comic book villain in a combat system that uses cards. The game is fun in single-player, local multi-player, and online multi-player modes. Pros: + Each hero and villain has a unique deck, giving each combination of heroes and villains a pretty unique feeling. In fact, each hero has a kind of "theme" that makes their gameplay style unique. Likewise for the villains. + UI is very well-designed. All the information you need is right there. You even have the option to rewind the game if you accidentally play a wrong card, or your action has unintended consequences. + Good level of challenge and balance. Some ability to customize the difficulty by changing the heroes, villain, environment, or switching to "advanced" mode. Cons: - The base game doesn't include very much content. The base game was almost a demo in my mind. However, I ended up liking it enough to buy the expansion packs, which vastly expand the number of heroes, villains, and environments to choose from.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: I own and enjoy the original Sentinels card game, plus one expansion. This version (the base, at least) is almost entirely faitfhful to the original. Where it isn't original, it offers variant versions of certain character decks. The UI is helpful, colorful. and loyal to the original game's art. Again, where it isn't totally faithful to the art, it adds more by depicting characters at different amounts of damage. For people who own the card game, this will really let you explore the game fully, because the computer takes away all the fiddly counters. Less time spent with setup, and book keeping, means more time spent playing. Due to this, I have gained a better understanding of the game, and enjoy it more. You should know this: The various combinations of heroes, environments, and villains can make the game nearly impossible to win, or ridiculously easy to win. Experience with the various decks will eventually guide you to the difficulty that you would like. On that note, Sentinels currently provides weekly scenarios for you to beat. It's nothing more than different combinations of decks, but like I said, that's what makes the game challenging.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: A TCG Board Game Turn based Superhero Game. Similar to the VS system Marvel tried for a few years with a slightly different game mechanic. Each player controls one or more heroes, while a villain and environment deck each run themselves. A given game includes 3 to 5 heroes, 1 villain and 1 environment, which can be mixed and matched to create a number of different scenarios. The core game comes with 10 heroes, 4 villains, and 4 environments. It has some wonderful pros and some cons. A: If you love the comics, the look, and superheroes in general. Then you will enjoy this game at any age B: The artwork and style is nicely executed. Though more serious comic fans may critisize the artwork as not graphic enough or of high grade. It gets the job done. C: Each Hero and villain has a purpose and the game has a solid structure to expand from. D: It has a narrative and a simple tutorial. E: Pow! Biff! Wam!, Interesting Character powers, mechanics and combinations. F; Alot of expansion potential, not just additional heroes and villains but adding some new mechanics to increase player choices in a turn. CONS A: It can be too distracting in its layout with too much going on. Not a modern version of comics layouts, more old style. The massive amount of colors can flatten its appearance than draw players eyes in. B: The animation mechanics, HP tracker and HP visual hurt the overall concept. It comes across cheaply done. The game could use a player customization and UI to allow players to re size the main screen, Increase and decrease patterns to make it more pleasable to their tastes. Something to consider. For example a Black and White version or making the HP of each big, for the eye impaired. C: If the game changable graphic and style wise in the future. Would vastly improve the game overall D: There is a difficultly scale that can get frustating. Like most TCGs expansions, they can be a trap for the same type of gaming experience. E; It's strength of simplisity is also its weakness. Heroes vs a Villain is nice, but after a while can get too redundant. You cannot just keep adding those two elements. OVERALL: More of a company attacking a main stream than creating something new. Sentinels will have plenty of the same type expansions and the game needs work. If you love superheroes, card games and combination gaming, then Sentinels is for you. Preview the game in Discussion, then hit VIDEO, see the gameplay at hand before buying, and look for this game on sale.  It has great potential, but hopefully is not limited by its one style artwork or same gameply or players will go on to something else.  It has its place, even though it does not wow you will beautiful graphic comic book art, like Magic the Gathering or other great comic book art, but it is a game that is very addicting. A great start to build off of. MY SCORE 3.8 out of 5 a good fun game.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse
text: This is the app this game needs, but is it app this game deserves? Reviewing both the game itself and the PC adaptation. PROS: - Unique, challenging villians that create interesting thematic challenges. - High difficulty ensures replayability. Game is not easily solvable. - Computer does all the game's bookkeeping for you. - Heroes and variants add onto gameplay variety. CONS: - Overwhelming number of modifiers and conditions to monitor. Things can get out of hand very quickly and it becomes difficult to work out what's happening in a turn. - Environments feel tacked on and don't evoke the setting they're trying to protray. - The game's mechanics drive the intensity of a match down. Things start of engaging and interesting, then become routine and formality as the Heroes finally get control of the situation. - Actual meaningful choice during a match is rare. Most decisions are just tests of your ability to calculate the optimal move. - Art is inconsisent and leans towards sloppy. PURCHASE CONSIDERATION TIDBIT: Core game feels a bit anemic. I'd advise buying at least one season alongside the core if this is a game that appeals to you. Would Recommend To: Comic book readers who are into turn based games and who are already familiar with the term "order of operations." Would Alternatively Suggest: PC Game Alternatives: Yomi (Dueling card game with cleaner mechanics and similar pay model), Tabletop Simulator with any of the games below. Board/Card Game Alternatives: Battlecon (Competitive turn based 1v1 fighting card game, dripping with theme and meaningful decision driven gameplay). Legendary or DC Comics Deck Building game (Licensed superhero card game. Theme is not delivered as well as Sentinels, but the games compensate by providing more interesting options during gameplay than Sentinels). Will thumb up ultimately because there's not a lot of PC accessible superhero card games and it is a fun game to play, despite it flaws. However, if any of my board game alternatives ever become a full fledged PC app themselves, I would thumb down this game for those alternative instead.

title: Sentinels of the Multiverse

I care a lot more about Legacy's story and struggles than I could care about Superman. If you are into card games and/or co-op multiplayer games, I strongly recommend Sentinels of the Multiverse.

title: Shadowgrounds
text: Shadowgrounds is an action over the head shooter from Frozenbyte that got a lot of mixed reviews so I got curious and had to review it myself as well. Indeed the game is a bag that can give you mixed feelings. The intro starts off wich seems to be the setting for your basic military experiment/conspiracy, which even though it has written low budget all over it, it still kind of sets the games premises on pretty good. The menu is looking ok as well and the background always keeps it a bit interesting and makes you hope something is going to happen . The first thing you will notice is that it DOES NOT have a save option.Yes, in this game you cannot save. You just have a couple of lives/respawns after wich it is game over. Like in the good old PlayStation Arcade games. This may put off a lot of people because the game can be surprisingly hard at some points, but for people like me it is a welcoming challenge. For all the others, well at least there is a save progress at the start of each level at least. The story starts off with the hero (Tyler) , a former military , current mechanic guy , beeng sent to fix some random generators with his buddies. The starting tone was very creepy and reminded me of a Dead Space atmosphere, which was great to notice, considering that this game is definetly not a triple A title. You fix the generators and notice that all the sudden there are bodies and blood everywhere,and surprisingly enough there is an alien invasion on your planet. You meet the army and start cleaning up. While not the most original type of story (has Doom 3) written all over it, the story holds up surprisingly well. Moving on to the characters. All of them, including Tyler, seem very under developed. The game tries to tell you something at the start to make you care,but it just fails to deliver or generally fails at the character development section. Graphic wise, everything seems decent, even though most of the graphics seem a bit washed up,even for a top down shooter. The details to the terrain/rooms are quite astonishing at some points. Overall the graphic,while not impressive in any way,does its job, just because of the attention to detail.The character models look just really low budget and plain dumb. The graphics type for the characters is really low quality compared to the overall graphics of the game. Music and sound FX. These just do their job but nothing more. No memorable music here and the SFX just blend in with the atmosphere. Some sound FX reminded me of the first Unreal game for some reason. The enemies, are your generic alien types and all are very annoying because they can just randomly appear in front of you and outnumber you directly. Their attack types get some time to get used to,and you do need some patience with each. You cannot just rush everything because you will die extremely fast. Gameplay and atmosphere. The game tries a dark and gritty atmosphere that initially delivers very well but it is just lost along the way. The flashlight object shadowing mechanic is very cool to look at but it gets old too quick. Overall the atmosphere is fairly decent, the game does tempt you to go back and finish it. Regarding gameplay only. It is quite satisfying to roll over large amounts of aliens but there are several points when it just feels unpolished. You need to do a lot of barrel rolling to avoid instant kill and you need to be aware of your environment all the time because if you hit a wall or an object,the character fails to respond quickly enough,and this causes a delay in movement,delay which will most of the time get you killed. This “stuck syndrome” is met in a large number of times,and really brings the game down as especially in the outdoor environments, you can get stuck a lot in the terrain because there are invisible walls in the middle of the map or the terrain was intended to be unpassable but on the map it looks just normal walking terrain. The gameplay overall feels initially good but gets repetitive and feels too hard at some points. The weapons to me were very disappointing. While the game does have some sort of upgrade system to keep things interesting, I found myself way too many times using the standard pistol with unlimited ammo because everything else has very scarce ammo. Speaking of weapons, most of them seem very ineffective to the aliens. You waste an entire magazine on one enemy at times. Now this beeing good or bad,it is debateble. It does add a survival element to the game, but this element feels like it just happen to be in the game. Does not seem an intended behaivour. The ammo supplies are low, the weapons are largely ineffective and the only thing that keeps this aspect up is the upgrade system,which turns like a chore fast. It’s does not feel crucial on what type of upgrades you need to take. Throughout the game you get upgrade parts to upgarde the weapons, which is a bit refreshing but again,gets old fast and also you find several computer terminals that fill in on the back story. After managing to finish the game, I realized that the atmospheric music was much better than what it was initially and also what seemed to be a generic military/alien invasion had quite an interesting twist in the end. The story seemed stale throught the game but the ending was really weird to witness. Also with the right upgrades,the weapons DO seem to deliver some punch ,but for me it was still a bit of a disappointment. I will recommend this game to fans of the genre and even to people that just want something new. Be advised, that the game is good but it is definetely not great, it does have the weight of a budget title all over it, but in the end it manages to deliver.

title: Shadowgrounds Survivor
text: was first released 7 years ago as a sequel to the original . It's a pretty well-made game, all about shooting hordes and hordes of pesky zombies from a top-down perspective. The story isn't remarkable in any way: three survivors of a massive alien attack try to "get out" in any way possible. Developer Frozenbyte has however improved upon the original in several ways. First of all, the three characters manage to come across as individuals, not as thirteen-in-a-dozen heroes, mostly thanks to the excellent voice-acting (although it's sometimes over-the-top, but better this than bland voices). Secondly, the weapons-arsenal is pretty neat, with a very distinctive "feel" about every weapon and individual weapons for all three character. Added to this is a well thought-out weapons- and character upgrade-system, which adds a light rpg-flavour to the game. Don't expect any keep of delving deep into weapons' customization or character builing, but still, it's pretty well done and really adds some much-needed depth to the gameplay. The original Shadowgrounds already had some solid graphics and these are markedly improved upon in Survivor. Especially light&shadows, explosions, fire effects (awesome flamethrower!!) and physics-effects are really impressive. Just as in the original, level-design is more than decent, with several items to search for and a logical built-up of each level. I found the game to be a tad short: after just under 5 hours I was through the singleplayer-campaign, not even having unlocked all of the character and weapons-upgrades. This can be done in the six unlockable missions where you have to keep alive for as long as possible, but since the leaderbords are dead now, that's fairly useless. Actually I wanted to play along for a bit longer, which is always a good sign. Alas, there have been seven years past since its release, so it seems like this little "franchise" will stay at two items forever. All in all, this is totally recommendable game for anyone who fancies shooting dozens of zombies in a no-brains way. I feel it's a bit expensive (7 euro at the moment) for a small-scale seven years' old game, but it gets discounts quite often, especially in a pack together with the original Shadowgrounds. Steam trading cards are a welcome addition too, Steam achievements are not here. Overall score: 7.5/10

text: Shadowgrounds was a pretty doesn't shooter a few years ago, but Survivor doesn't really do much new, and is pretty boring. As a top down shooter you play as a marine who is trying to escape a ruined base that is overrun by aliens. The weapons are pretty generic with shotguns, assault rifles, flamethrowers, grenades etc. You can pick up health packs, ammo, and OK you know this formula already. You can easily kill these guys and it doesn't feel very satisfying at all. You can shoot barrels, toss grenades, or just run around holding the fire button and you'll beat these guys. Ammo is plentiful so you never feel like you're "surviving" and it's pretty hard to die. There is an upgrade system that you use by finding "parts" and when you level up you can use points for different upgrades like sonar, health boosts etc., and each character you play has the same upgrades? The game is fun however since it's good for more casual players who don't like the intensity of other top down shooters, but even the aliens are generic looking. Instead of creepy deformed things you just get typical bug like aliens. The game doesn't look or sound too good either, and the music almost seems non existent while the game looks pretty bland. The level design is also pretty bad since I wandered around areas and didn't know where to go like shooting a glass panel to open a walkway. title: Shadows: Heretic Kingdoms
text: Excellent ARPG. I'm one of the half dozen or so people who purchased the classic ARPG Heretic Kingdoms at release and enjoyed it quite a bit, so I was excited for this somewhat belated semi-sequel (same world, different characters). It really delivers. It has all the appeal of the original and its bizarre, dark anti-theistic world of the Heretic Kingdoms setting as well as great art design and graphics, rock solid controls and an interesting combat mechanic whereby you can change to a different character/form on the fly. Each form has different strengths and weaknesses and multiple ones are frequently viable in a given area. Bosses are fun, enemies are challenging without being overly difficult and all-in-all this is just a great game. Just an FYI, this game series is single-player and campaign oriented and plays more like the Dungeon Siege or Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance than the more loot-driven, frequently multi-player oriented games like the Diablo series or Titan Quest. Additionally, Book 2 has not been released. Even if it never is, it's still a great game and the ending doesn't feel abrupt. If you like ARPG's, buy it.

text: I usually do not like ARPGs, and skipped this one by due to not being interested in arpgs and thinking the "shadow world" mechanic sounded bad.   I bought this while bored and was very suprised by how much i liked it.  It is a very well done game.  Clearing every area twice isn't so bad.  I like my demon and my main guy so far, I enjoy the charcater building and there being no resets of skill points requiring thought. Combat is fast and slow, with almost limitless heals and sometimes extremem damage spikes to help with the mechanics.  It has just the right challenge level and combat is very well done considering you have potions, 3 alive people to cycle through, the demon, and your soul bar heals and reserrects. The game has a pretty decent crafting system.  The rpg aspects of quests and npc interactions are actually very heavy for an ARPG and plays like a real crpg.  Production value is high and the voice overs are actually really good for the demon, my fighter character, and the others I've heard. I am happy i bought this game, even at the current full price of $20.  I just bought the orginal and am going to play that through now and then come back to this.  I skipped almost all arpgs back in the day like this and sacred, etc, but am now learning to appreciate the heavier ones like Divine Divinity. For some reason this game, S:HK reminds me of Lionheart.  It isn't very similar but it has repetetive combat that somehow doesn't bother me.  This is a different sort of game than the ones I usually go for so is hard for me to recommend it to people who usually play crpgs, but I think most crpg fans will find this to be a good game whereas Torchlight, Diablo 3 type arpg fans may think it is to crpgish and slow.

title: Shadows: Heretic Kingdoms
text: This game is really awesome! Great take on the classic RPG. Allows you to transform at will into different characters with different abilities. So for those who are always conflicted about whether to be a mage, brawler, or archer at the beginning of RPGs, don't worry because you get all of them at some point in the game as you devour souls. Graphics, story, and voice overs are all solid. Not sure why there are some people who dislike this game. The only gripe I had was that the load times were long. Shadows has become one of my favorite games, and for $20 it's much cheaper than many big name RPGs.

title: Shadows: Heretic Kingdoms
text: While the game has great visuals, impressive voice acting (in as much as they've implemented so far), good music, great atmosphere and apparent character choices the controls kill it for me. Some would say that controls are only part of the game, but to them I say, it's one of the few things that you have to deal with for the entirety of the game. It's not something to take lightly. At Shadows: Heretic Kingdoms' current price it comes off as a tough sale even if this game has a lot of promise. If you're really into ARPG's you might have a difficult time over-looking them. If you're casual ARPG player, this may not affect you at all. I would keep your eye on this and when people stop complaining about "sluggish" controls, it would make the price a lot easier to swallow. This isn't a title to write off.
